title: Whether theology is a speculative or a practical discipline
pass_a_gloss: Article XXVIII. Whether theology is a speculative or a practical discipline. 1. In this controversy philosophers' and theologians' opinions vary. Some make theology merely speculative; others merely practical; others mixed. 2. We: wayfarers' theology is principally practical, because its ultimate end is not bare contemplation, but enjoyment of God through faith, hope, charity, and obedience — although many speculative things are contained in it. 3. The theology of the homeland is more speculative or contemplative, because it terminates in the vision of God. Yet even in the way theology does not exclude speculation; but it orders it to the practice of piety.
pass_b_english: Article XXVIII. Whether theology is a speculative or a practical discipline.
1. Opinions vary: merely speculative, merely practical, or mixed.

2. Wayfarers' theology is principally practical — its ultimate end is not bare contemplation but enjoyment of God through faith, hope, charity, and obedience — though it contains much that is speculative.
3. Homeland theology is more speculative or contemplative, ending in God's vision. Even in the way, theology does not shut out speculation; it orders it to the practice of piety.
source_text:
ART. XXVIII.
Utrum Theologia sit disciplina speculativa, an practica.

1. In hac controversia variae sunt Philosophorum & Theologorum sententiae. Alii Theologiam mere speculativam; alii mere practicam; alii mixtam faciunt.

2. Nos: Theologia viatorum est principaliter practica, quia finis ejus ultimus non est nuda contemplatio, sed fruitio DEI per fidem, spem, charitatem, & obedientiam — etsi multa in ea speculativa continentur.

3. Theologia patriae est magis speculativa seu contemplativa, quia in visione DEI terminatur. Attamen etiam in via Theologia non excludit speculationem; sed ordinat eam ad praxim pietatis.
